solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Perfunctory choice of academics

parts.note: a prof, short for professor, is one kind of academic
or is the word that offers a choice between two things
an MA, a Master of Arts, is another kind of academic

explanation.surface: A dull, box-ticking selection made by university staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'academics' is used twice over, giving two different university people, a professor and a master's graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: Done as a matter of form only, so a token, routine gesture is a perfunctory one.

clue.text: Fairy Queen's purse

definitions.note: a verb here: to draw the lips together

parts.note: Puck is the mischievous fairy of A Midsummer Night's Dream
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: Titania, the fairy queen, and her handbag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purse' looks like a noun, a bag, but it is the verb for tightening the lips.
explanation.definitionFit: To pucker the lips is to gather them tightly together, the same action as pursing.

clue.text: Strange, but étoile is black hole

indicators.note: strange suggests something altered and unfamiliar, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An astronomy oddity: a star, étoile in French, that is really a black hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black hole' wants to be astronomy; it is a dark dungeon.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret dungeon reached by a trapdoor, a pitch-dark pit where prisoners were forgotten.

clue.text: Rarely heard solitary miscreant on display tonight

indicators.note: heard says the words for a lone wrongdoer are taken by their sound, not their spelling

parts.note: solitary gives one and a miscreant's offence is a sin, so one sin
an occasional second full moon in a month, a blue moon, shown in tonight's sky

explanation.surface: A lone wrongdoer, seldom heard of, is on show tonight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one sin' said aloud runs together as the first two words; 'on display tonight' describes the rare moon itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for something happening very seldom, after the rare second full moon in a month.

clue.text: Highly unlikely it could be Simba in the distance

definitions.text: Highly unlikely it could be Simba in the distance

parts.words: Highly unlikely it could be Simba in the distance
parts.note: Simba is the lion of The Lion King, and a far-off big cat could be read as a lion a mil away

explanation.surface: Spotting the famous cartoon lion on a distant horizon would be very improbable.
explanation.walkthrough: A mil is a tiny unit of length, so a distant LION becomes MIL LION; the phrase gives long odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds so long that the event is practically impossible, a turn of phrase for improbability.

clue.text: Bank Arabs use a lot for capital

indicators.note: using a lot of the words, but not all of them, means a run of letters is taken from inside them

explanation.surface: Arab banks making heavy use of some city's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'use a lot' says most of 'Bank Arabs' is used: drop the first B and the final BS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankara is the capital city of Turkey.

clue.text: No way for Navy to demand sunshine without first dodging storm

indicators.note: storm suggests turbulence, so the letters are thrown into a new order
first picks out the opening letter of the word dodging

explanation.surface: Refusing to let sailors demand fine weather while they dodge a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without first dodging' removes a D from the letters of 'for Navy to demand sunshine'; 'storm' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for something that will never happen at all, an emphatic refusal.

clue.text: Leads a choir rehearsing in D sharp

indicators.note: leads means the front letters of each of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A conductor runs a choir practice in the key of D sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharp' wants to be part of the musical key; it is the definition, and D is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrid smell or taste is bitter and pungent, harsh on the nose or tongue.

clue.text: A rat claims he's raised the bar

indicators.note: claims means takes in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a louse, like a rat, is a contemptible person

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the letters read upwards, so in reverse

parts.note: the word he supplies the letters, with its 's as a link

explanation.surface: A traitor boasts that he has raised standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rat' is a person here, not a rodent; the 's of 'he's' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a pub, where the bar is the room serving drinks.

clue.text: A guess is bad manners

indicators.note: a bad version of something is spoiled or wrong, so the letters come out in another order

explanation.surface: Merely guessing at an answer is poor etiquette.
explanation.definitionFit: Usages are customs or habitual practices, the conventional ways of behaving.

clue.text: Measuring volume of disco regularly, putting youngster first

indicators.note: putting the youngster first means it comes before the other piece

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a junior scout

indicators.note: taking letters regularly means every other letter of the word disco

explanation.surface: Turning up the disco's sound now and then, letting the kids go first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd and 4th letters of 'disco', I and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubic describes a measurement in three dimensions, as in cubic metres, the units of volume.

clue.text: Lines indicating air is nearly gone

definitions.text: Lines indicating air is nearly gone

parts.words: Lines indicating air is nearly gone
parts.note: the air is a song or tune, and the lines that show it is almost over are its closing stanza

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a gauge showing a diver's oxygen running out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' suggests breathing, but here it is a tune; the lines are the words of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing stanza of a song or hymn tells you the tune is about to end.

clue.text: Producing dramatic literary openings not unknown

indicators.note: not unknown says the unknown letter is to be removed, with the literary openings going in its place

parts.note: something dramatic is exciting
X is the classic algebraic unknown
the openings of the word literary are its first letters, L and I

explanation.surface: A writing class turning out thrilling first lines, with nothing left obscure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not unknown' takes the X out of EXCITING, and the first two letters of 'literary' go into the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out or bring forth, so eliciting a reaction is producing one.

clue.text: Event where the winner gets the most bucks

definitions.text: Event where the winner gets the most bucks

parts.words: Event where the winner gets the most bucks
parts.note: bucks here are leaps by horses or bulls as well as dollars of prize money

explanation.surface: Looks like a competition with the biggest cash prize going to the champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bucks' reads as dollars, but the second sense is a bucking animal throwing its rider.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy contest of riding bucking broncos and bulls is a classic American show.

clue.text: Mark pens first rate song

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a stain is a mark

indicators.note: first indicates the opening letter of the word rate

explanation.surface: A critic's note: grade the pens first, then judge the song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' puts R, the first letter of 'rate', inside STAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a passage of music or a melody, as in 'the strains of a waltz'.

clue.text: See 6
One's trying to get away by 6 — pack anti-left-wing circular

parts.note: a six-pack is a set of well-defined abdominal muscles, called abs
con, as in pros and cons, means against

indicators.note: circular means going round, so the left-wing word is turned back to front

parts.note: red is the colour of left-wing politics

explanation.surface: An escaper with a six-pack handing out an anti-socialist leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: The 6 makes 'pack' a six-pack, ABS; 'circular' turns RED into DER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who flees, especially from justice, is trying to make a getaway.

clue.text: Hide lover's desire during endless provocative dance

indicators.note: during means the desire piece goes inside the dance piece
endless means the final letter of the dance word is cut off

parts.note: twerking is a sexually provocative dance with thrusting hips
an itch is a restless desire

explanation.surface: Someone longs to conceal a lover during a racy dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb; it is the noun, a birdwatchers' shelter. 'endless' cuts TWERK to TWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A keen birdwatcher, who loves sitting in a hide waiting to spot rare birds.

clue.text: Partial lift-off by Armstrong, maybe?

parts.note: Armstrong suggests the astronaut Neil, but Lance Armstrong the cyclist could raise only a front wheel

explanation.surface: Seems to describe an aborted rocket launch with Neil Armstrong aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The astronaut is the false path; the cyclist Lance Armstrong lifts just one end of his bike.
explanation.definitionFit: A stunt riding a bicycle with its front wheel in the air is only half off the ground.

clue.text: By far extremes of anarchy lies chaos

indicators.note: chaos means disorder, so the letters are mixed up
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A political slogan: chaos lies at the far ends of anarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: A and Y, the ends of 'anarchy', are shuffled with LIES.
explanation.definitionFit: As in winning easily the best: a comfortable margin, by a wide distance.

clue.text: Take in old man with tablets back to front

indicators.note: back to front means the final letter of the name is moved round to the start

parts.note: Moses brought the stone tablets of the Ten Commandments down from Sinai

explanation.surface: An elderly patient who must swallow pills, taken in reverse order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' moves the last S of MOSES to the front, giving SMOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To osmose is to absorb by osmosis, soaking something up through a membrane.

clue.text: Using second cue, hit a terrible long shot

indicators.note: a terrible shot goes all wrong, so the letters scramble

explanation.surface: A snooker player borrows a spare cue and plays an awful long pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long shot' looks like part of the snooker scene; it is the definition, meaning a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A long shot is an attempt with little hope of success, a slim possibility.

clue.text: See 20 down
See 4
Turnaround of character needed after cricket match disgrace

indicators.note: after puts the reversed letter behind the match

parts.note: an ODI is a One Day International, a limited-overs cricket match

indicators.note: turnaround means the Greek letter is read backwards

parts.note: mu is a character, a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A player's character must be rebuilt after a shameful cricket defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is a Greek letter, not a person's nature; ODI is a One Day International.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is the general hatred and disrepute that falls on someone who has done wrong.

clue.text: Hot IT man's corrected bug

indicators.note: something corrected has been put into a different, proper order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An overheated computer technician has fixed a software glitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' wants to be a computer fault; it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The satin moth is a white moth, and bug is a loose everyday word for any insect.

clue.text: People start hysterical cries about election

indicators.note: start picks out the opening letter of the word hysterical
about means surrounding, so the cries go round the other piece

parts.note: oi is a shouted cry, so two cries give it twice
a poll is a vote or an election

explanation.surface: A crowd begins shrieking at the result of a vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts POLL inside the two OIs, after H from 'start hysterical'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek phrase for the common people or the masses, the general populace.

clue.text: Wore ragged

definitions.meaning: to have clothes on is to be wearing them
to rag someone, in British slang, is to tease or kid them, which is also to have them on

explanation.surface: Clothes worn into tatters.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: dressed in something, and having fooled or teased someone.

clue.text: Detention given by master during break

indicators.note: during means the master piece goes within the break piece

parts.note: to rend is to tear apart or break
MA, Master of Arts, is a master's degree

explanation.surface: A teacher keeps a pupil in at break time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detention' and 'break' suggest school; the sense is legal custody, and 'break' means tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner held in custody awaiting trial is in custody on a court's order.

clue.text: Play banned player out of necessity

indicators.note: banned means the player is thrown out of the longer word

parts.note: a performance is a play staged for an audience
a man is a player in a team or on a chessboard

explanation.surface: A sports report: a game played without its suspended star, because it had to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banned' removes MAN from PERFORMANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal adverb meaning by force of circumstance, because it cannot be helped.
